title: Canonical closed restriction by clopen idempotent localization
statement:
Let $R$ be a commutative ring, $P$ a profinite space (compact Hausdorff and totally disconnected), and $g:\operatorname{Spec}R\to P$ a continuous map [def-weil-affine-spectrum]. For a closed subset $Z\subseteq P$, index by its clopen neighborhoods $U$ in reverse inclusion. Let $e_U$ be the unique idempotent with $D(e_U)=g^{-1}(U)$ [lem-weil-pbc-spec-clopen-idempotent], and form
$$R_Z=\varinjlim_{U\supseteq Z}R[1/e_U]$$
in commutative $R$-algebras [def-weil-ring-localization-away, def-weil-pbc-category-colimit], with the unique $R$-algebra transition maps when $V\subseteq U$. These maps exist and define a small nonempty directed diagram. The subset $M_Z=\{e_U:U\supseteq Z\text{ clopen}\}$ is multiplicative, and the canonical maps induce an $R$-algebra isomorphism $R_Z\cong M_Z^{-1}R$, where the latter is the ring of fractions with denominators in $M_Z$ [lem-weil-pbc-ring-localization-universal-property]. Contraction of primes identifies $\operatorname{Spec}R_Z$ homeomorphically with $g^{-1}(Z)$, with its subspace topology. If $q\in\operatorname{Spec}R_Z$ corresponds to $x\in g^{-1}(Z)$, the canonical map $R_x\to(R_Z)_q$ is an isomorphism [def-weil-pbc-localization-at-prime]. For closed $Z\subseteq Z'$, inclusion of neighborhood diagrams induces a canonical map $R_{Z'}\to R_Z$; these maps compose, their spectrum maps are the inclusions $g^{-1}(Z)\subseteq g^{-1}(Z')$, and their localized maps become the identity on $R_x$ under the displayed canonical isomorphisms whenever $g(x)\in Z$.

source.place: Tag 097C, lemma-construct, proof: canonical colimit of idempotent localizations; the explicit localization and natural local-ring identifications expand the blueprint Preliminaries.

proof.text: Let $I_Z=\{U\subseteq P:U\text{ is clopen},\ Z\subseteq U\}$, with one arrow $U\to V$ when $V\subseteq U$. It is a set of subsets of $P$, hence small in the ambient universe fixed by the size convention. It is nonempty since $P\in I_Z$. For $U,V\in I_Z$, the clopen $U\cap V$ is again in $I_Z$ and receives arrows from both. There are no distinct parallel arrows in this poset category. Thus the diagram index is nonempty and directed (and filtered).

source.place: Preliminaries: clopen neighbourhood index, made explicit

proof.text: Continuity of $g$ makes $g^{-1}(U)$ clopen, so the clopen-idempotent bijection supplies its unique $e_U$. The product $e_Ue_V$ is idempotent, and primality gives $D(e_Ue_V)=D(e_U)\cap D(e_V)=g^{-1}(U\cap V)$. Uniqueness therefore gives $e_{U\cap V}=e_Ue_V$; similarly $e_P=1$ since $D(1)=\operatorname{Spec}R$. Hence $M_Z$ contains $1$ and is closed under multiplication. When $V\subseteq U$, the same formula gives $e_Ue_V=e_V$.

source.place: Preliminaries: clopen idempotents; product and unit formulas from uniqueness

proof.text: For $V\subseteq U$, $e_Ue_V=e_V$ implies that the image of $e_U$ in $R[1/e_V]$ is $1$, by multiplying by the inverse of $e_V$. The localization universal property gives a unique $R$-algebra map $\rho_{UV}:R[1/e_U]\to R[1/e_V]$. Its formula is $a/e_U^n\mapsto(a/1)(e_U/1)^{-n}$. Identity maps and composites are the required maps because they agree on $R$, and uniqueness for localization at the powers of $e_U$ makes them equal. Thus these maps define the claimed diagram.

source.place: Tag 00CP, proposition-universal-property-localization, applied to powers of the idempotents

proof.text: Put $L=M_Z^{-1}R$ and let $\lambda:R\to L$ be its localization map. Since every $e_U$ is inverted in $L$, the universal property gives $R$-algebra maps $\kappa_U:R[1/e_U]\to L$. They form a cocone: $\kappa_V\rho_{UV}$ and $\kappa_U$ agree on $R$, hence are equal. For any cocone $\mu_U:R[1/e_U]\to A$ in commutative $R$-algebras, write $f:R\to A$ for its structure map. For every $U$, $f(e_U)=\mu_U(e_U/1)$ is a unit. Hence there is a unique $R$-algebra map $h:L\to A$ with $h\lambda=f$. For each $U$, $h\kappa_U$ and $\mu_U$ agree on $R$, so localization uniqueness gives $h\kappa_U=\mu_U$. Conversely any cocone factorization is an $R$-algebra map and thus must be this $h$. Consequently $(L,\kappa_U)$ is a colimit: this also proves existence without assuming any general colimit-existence theorem. Uniqueness of colimits identifies the specified $R_Z$ canonically with $L$, intertwining every coprojection and the map from $R$.

source.place: Tag 00CP, proposition-universal-property-localization; expansion of Tag 097C, proetale.tex lemma-construct, last sentence

proof.text: A point of $Z$ lies in every $U\in I_Z$. Conversely, if $p\in P\setminus Z$, the clopen basis theorem applied to the open $P\setminus Z$ gives a clopen $W$ with $p\in W\subseteq P\setminus Z$. Then $U=P\setminus W$ belongs to $I_Z$ and does not contain $p$. Thus $\bigcap_{U\in I_Z}U=Z$. All hypotheses of the basis theorem are exactly the compact Hausdorff and total disconnectedness hypotheses on $P$.

source.place: Tag 08ZZ, lemma-profinite-refine-open-covering, via its clopen-basis consequence

proof.text: Apply the arbitrary-multiplicative-localization spectrum theorem to $L=M_Z^{-1}R$. Contraction is a homeomorphism onto the subspace of primes $x$ disjoint from $M_Z$. Such an $x$ satisfies $e_U\notin x$ for every $U\in I_Z$, equivalently $g(x)\in U$ for every $U\in I_Z$, equivalently $g(x)\in Z$ by step 5. Through the canonical $R$-algebra isomorphism of step 4 this is precisely the asserted homeomorphism $\operatorname{Spec}R_Z\simeq g^{-1}(Z)$, given by contraction, with the stated subspace topology.

source.place: Tag 00E3, lemma-spec-localization; applied to the explicit localization from step 4

proof.text: Let $q\in\operatorname{Spec}R_Z$ and let $x$ be its contraction. Under step 4 the structure map $\lambda_Z:R\to R_Z$ is a localization at $M_Z$: its fractions and equality relation give conditions (a), (b), (c) in the cited localization-prime theorem. Apply clause (2) of that theorem with $A=R$, $A'=R_Z$, $W=M_Z$, $\mathfrak q'=q$, $\mathfrak q=x$. It gives exactly the canonical isomorphism $\alpha_{Z,x}:R_x\xrightarrow{\sim}(R_Z)_q$, $a/s\mapsto\lambda_Z(a)/\lambda_Z(s)$ for $s\notin x$. In particular the assertion concerns the induced local map itself, not an unspecified abstract isomorphism.

source.place: Tag 00C9, item-localization-localization; Tag 00E3, lemma-spec-localization; canonical local-ring formula of lem-weil-pbc-localization-prime-residue-field-iso (2)

proof.text: For closed $Z\subseteq Z'$, every clopen neighbourhood of $Z'$ is a clopen neighbourhood of $Z$. Restrict the $R_Z$ cocone to $I_{Z'}$ and use the colimit property to obtain $\phi_{Z',Z}:R_{Z'}\to R_Z$. Under step 4 it is the unique map $M_{Z'}^{-1}R\to M_Z^{-1}R$ fixing $R$, since $M_{Z'}\subseteq M_Z$; in fractions it sends $a/e$ to $a/e$. Identity and composite maps fix $R$ and therefore coincide with the corresponding canonical maps by localization uniqueness. For a prime $q$ of $R_Z$ its inverse image $q'$ in $R_{Z'}$ contracts to the same prime $x$ in $R$. The homeomorphisms of step 6 consequently identify the spectrum map with the inclusion $g^{-1}(Z)\subseteq g^{-1}(Z')$.
